description: Able to recognize and describe both the theoretical and practical aspects of computing with images. Able to describe the foundation of image formation and image analysis. Understand the geometric relationships between 2D images and the 3D world. Have gained exposure to motion, matching, recognition, extraction, and categorization from images.

syllabus.title: Introduction and Digital Image Formation
syllabus.body: Fundamentals of image formation, what is computer vision, a brief history; geometric camera models, geometric camera calibration, radiometry, measuring light, shadows and shading, color.

syllabus.title: Early Vision - Multiple Images
syllabus.body: The geometry of multiple views, stereopsis, affine structure from motion, projective structure from motion; feature detection and matching: points and patches, edges, lines.

syllabus.title: Mid Level Vision
syllabus.body: Segmentation by clustering, segmentation by fitting a model, segmentation and fitting using probabilistic methods, tracking with linear dynamic models; feature-based alignment: 2D and 3D, pose estimation, geometric intrinsic calibration.

syllabus.title: High Level Vision - Geometric Methods
syllabus.body: Model-based vision, smooth surfaces and their outlines, aspect graphs, range data; structure from motion: triangulation, two-frame structure from motion, factorization, bundle adjustment, constrained structure and motion; probabilistic and inferential methods, image based rendering.

syllabus.title: Dense Motion Estimation and Recognition
syllabus.body: Translational alignment, parametric motion, spline-based motion, optical flow, layered motion; 3D reconstruction: shape from X, active range finding, surface representations, model-based reconstruction, recovering texture maps; recognition: object detection, face recognition, instance recognition, category recognition, context and scene understanding.

outcomes: Understand the basics of 2D and 3D Computer Vision.
Design and describe various methods used for motion, registration, alignment, detection, recognition and matching in images.
referenceBooks: Rafael C. Gonzalez and Richard E. Woods, Digital Image Processing, Fourth Edition, Pearson, 2018.
Forsyth and Ponce, Computer Vision: A Modern Approach, Second Edition, Pearson, 2015.
Richard Szeliski, Computer Vision: Algorithms and Applications, Springer-Verlag, 2010.
